factChecks.claim: Airbnb introduced categories organized around home style, location, and nearby activities.
Categories help people recognize possibilities before they can name a destination.

shareValue: A three-question test for helping users discover options they cannot name yet.

source.title: A new Airbnb for a new world of travel

caption: Airbnb Categories addresses a search problem that begins before the search box.

slides.text: Airbnb designed search for people who cannot name the destination.
A search box assumes the answer is already known.
slides.kicker: But a traveler may know the feeling—beachfront, cabin, design—before knowing the city.
Instead of only asking where, Airbnb organized homes around style, location, and nearby activities.

items: Known intent: search for the answer
New possibility: discover what was hard to name

slides.text: Sometimes users do not need a better search box.
slides.kicker: They need a vocabulary for possibilities they have not discovered yet.

items: What can users describe but not name?

captions.instagram:
Airbnb Categories addresses a problem that starts before typing: sometimes people know the kind of experience they want, but not the destination to search for.

Airbnb's launch described categories organized around a home's style, location, or nearby activities. That turns search from pure retrieval into guided discovery.

The broader product lesson: when users cannot name the answer, help them recognize useful qualities first. Save the final slide for your next navigation or marketplace review.

Where does your product expect users to know too much before they begin?

Source: Airbnb, A new Airbnb for a new world of travel (2022)
